findings.description: SHEET-MARK-003's clause "recording the symbol degraded (no mark) only after it stays non-numeric past the bounded retry window" reads naturally as: prolonged non-numeric status eventually forces a no-mark/degraded outcome. All three A-implementations, working from the text alone, encode exactly that — once the window is exceeded, the symbol unconditionally clears its cache and becomes degraded (A1: `self.cached = None; MarkOutcome::Degraded` in the `else` branch, no check on prior cache state; A2: `self.last_good = None; MarkOutcome::Degraded`, same unconditional clear; A3: `if consecutive_bad_polls > MAX_RETRIES { cached_cents = None; degraded = true; }`, also unconditional). The REAL code does the opposite whenever a prior mark exists: `read_marks` carries the prior `Mark` (identical `price_cents` AND `quote_date`, never re-stamped) forward and explicitly does NOT record it degraded (`transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window` asserts `produced.degraded.get("AMZN").is_none()` even after `client.read_count() == 4 == max_polls`). Worse, this carry-forward has no cross-cycle expiration at all: the `prior` map fed into one cycle's `read_marks` is exactly the previous cycle's output, so a symbol that gets one good quote and then stays transient forever will carry that same stamp indefinitely and NEVER be recorded degraded — proven end-to-end by `cycle.rs::marks_read_back_are_cached_and_injected_into_the_next_replay` (AMZN's cycle-1 mark of 170.00/quote_date 19_180 survives unchanged into cycle 2 while transient). SHEET-MARK-003's "bounded retry window" text gives no hint that the bound applies only to a single settle pass's poll count and never to how many consecutive cycles a symbol may ride a stale prior mark — the one point where all three independent A-runs guessed the same (wrong, relative to code) thing is strong evidence the spec text under-specifies this and, read literally, points the other way.

The code carves out a third reading state, `PriceReading::Permanent` ("a terminal non-numeric error, usually a ticker-form mismatch"), with rules opposite to the transient case that SHEET-MARK-003 actually describes: it settles the poll loop immediately (no retry consumed) and is ALWAYS recorded degraded with reason `DegradeReason::Permanent` — with NO carry-forward of any prior mark even when one exists. `permanent_error_degrades_immediately_no_prior_carry` proves a `BADX` symbol with a prior $10.00 mark is dropped, not carried, the instant a `Permanent` reading appears, and settles in fewer than `max_polls` reads. SHEET-MARK-003's text names only the transient case ("#N/A"/"Loading...") and is silent on any terminal-error variant; all three B-runs independently flagged this as a deliberate "contrast case" to the rule the spec text does state.

"Bounded retry window" is pinned to a concrete discrete-poll-count mechanism — `SettleConfig.max_polls: u32` (default `8`, exercised at 2/3/4/8 across the tests), counted across repeated calls to `client.read_price_pass()` within one settle pass — never a wall-clock duration. The settle loop breaks exactly at `polls >= cfg.max_polls` (verified: `max_polls=3` → exactly 3 reads in `settle_pass_is_bounded_by_max_polls`). SHEET-MARK-003 never states the window is poll-count- rather than time-based; tellingly, two of the three A-runs (A1, A2), reasoning from the text alone, assumed a wall-clock `Instant`/`Duration` model instead of a poll count, only A3 guessed the count-based mechanism the real code actually uses.

A transport-level failure of the read call itself (`client.read_price_pass()` returning `Err`) is handled entirely differently from a per-symbol non-numeric cell: `read_marks` propagates the `Err` and produces NO `MarksProduced` at all — not even an empty one — specifically so it never looks like "all symbols degraded" (per the doc comment and `transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks`); carry-forward on transport failure is left entirely to the caller (`runtime`), not to this function. SHEET-MARK-003 talks only about the content of a `Price` cell and says nothing about the read call itself failing or this propagate-vs-carry split. All three B-runs called this out as a distinct, unwanted-behavior-level rule.

A symbol entirely absent from a given poll's returned `PricePass` is treated identically to an explicit `Transient` reading for settlement purposes (the settled check is `!matches!(latest.get(s), Some(PriceReading::Transient) | None)`), though within one settle pass it retains its last-observed reading across polls rather than reverting to "unknown" each time it's missing. SHEET-MARK-003 only names `#N/A`/`Loading...` cell contents and never addresses a symbol being missing from the poll results altogether; all three B-runs state this rule (B3 most precisely: "a symbol missing from a given poll retains its previously observed reading rather than reverting to unknown").

Secondary instability, not itself a finding: A1/A2 assume the retry window is wall-clock time while A3 assumes a fixed poll count, and A1 additionally diverges from A2/A3 by degrading immediately on the very first transient reading when no prior mark exists (rather than retrying within the window as A2/A3 and the real code do). All three runs flagged these as invented, spec-silent choices rather than spec-forced facts, so per the classification rule they aren't independent findings — but the split confirms (from the other side) that the spec's "bounded retry window" phrase is genuinely underspecified enough to produce divergent guesses, one of which (A3's) happens to match the real mechanism and two of which (A1/A2's) do not.
